A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the triplet supercurrents are generated by the magnetic field-orientation-dependent spin-mixing processes in Josephson junction with exchange-spring interfaces.

we have shown that the triplet supercurrents can be tuned by the magnetic field direction and magnitude, and that the triplet superconducting coherence length is much longer than the singlet coherence length.
the magnetic Josephson junction with exchange-spring interface is a promising candidate for the generation of triplet supercurrents and for the realization of a spintronic Josephson junction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the triplet supercurrents can be controlled by an external magnetic field.
the magnetic field orientation can be used to control the magnitude and sign of the supercurrent.
the triplet supercurrent is strongly dependent on the direction of the external magnetic field, which can be used for the realization of spintronic devices.
